Articles.Title: Right Answer, Wrong Reasons: AI Forecasts Costco - Hassan El Mghari & Omar El Mghari, Together AI｜AI Engineer - finance.biggo.com

stories.Headline: Codenotary Releases Open-Source AgentMon Live to Improve AI Coding Productivity
stories.Summary:
Codenotary, a company focused on the safe and secure use of AI, released AgentMon Live on November 9, 2026, as free, open-source software for developers who use Claude Code. The tool checks whether AI coding agents have actually finished the work they were asked to do, flags problems that need a human's attention, and aims to reduce wasted token consumption. It is available immediately under the Apache 2.0 license, which gives developers access to the source code so they can inspect, modify, extend, and contribute to it. Codenotary describes the release as its contribution to the growing community of developers building software with agentic AI.

AgentMon Live connects directly to Claude Code and offers a live dashboard showing agent activity, tool use, file changes, and verification results. Its "Done Gate" feature examines recorded session activity for signs of unfinished work, such as failed or outdated tests, incomplete tasks, and subagent failures, before an agent is allowed to finish. An optional second-model advisor can separately assess whether the agent's response addresses the developer's original request. The dashboard also shows active tools, subagents, pending approvals, and stalled or repeatedly failing processes, so developers need not read agent conversations continuously. The software further reports on token consumption, context growth, cache efficiency, and tool execution time, and it flags possible inefficiencies such as repeated file reads and unused Model Context Protocol servers.

Codenotary's chief technology officer and co-founder, Dennis Zimmer, said that productivity from AI coding should be measured by how much useful, verified work gets done. He argued that developers should not have to spend their days supervising agents, confirming that they really finished, or guessing where their tokens went. Zimmer said the company is releasing the tool free and open source because it believes the whole agentic development community should benefit. The announcement also notes that agents may report completion even when tests have failed, when verification predates the latest code changes, or when required steps remain undone.

The software works with Claude Code version 2.1.308 and later, and developers can install it from within Claude Code using a plugin command that references the codenotary/agentmon-live marketplace entry. Source code, installation instructions, and contribution information are published on GitHub at github.com/codenotary/agentmon-live. The articles do not say how many developers have adopted the tool or whether Codenotary plans further releases. The announcement appeared on SD Times, which also carried several unrelated items about AI and software development in the same feed.

Articles.Title: Codenotary Releases Open-Source AgentMon Live to Improve AI Coding Productivity - SD Times

stories.Headline: Kong launches Token Vault to secure AI agent access
stories.Summary:
Kong has launched Token Vault for Kong Identity, a product now generally available that is designed to control how AI agents reach enterprise systems. The release was reported on 9 November 2026. Token Vault brokers downstream credentials at runtime, so agents can reach APIs, MCP servers, models, data and other authorised resources without ever holding the underlying secrets. The launch responds to companies giving AI agents wider roles across internal systems, applications and data stores. Each of those systems often requires its own authentication method, which leaves organisations managing a growing number of credentials tied to software agents.

That sprawl raises the risk of misuse if an agent is compromised, misconfigured or behaves unexpectedly, since persistent credentials could let an agent act across several systems faster than a human operator could respond. Under Kong's model, an agent first authenticates with its own identity, Kong Identity then decides what it may access, and Token Vault supplies the needed credential only when an authorised request is sent. Kong presents the centralised approach as a way to make credential management and revocation easier, reduce exposure of secrets and avoid building separate credential logic for each new integration. Token Vault extends Kong Identity from identification and authentication into a wider access model covering identification, authorisation and credential brokering. It can also work alongside Kong's gateways and policy enforcement tools, so an organisation can handle agent identity, access decisions, credential brokering, policy enforcement and audit activity within one architecture.

Reza Shafii, Senior Vice President, Product at Kong, said enterprises need to widen what agents can reach without widening the credentials those agents hold, and that keeping downstream credentials under central control makes that possible. The launch is aimed at security and identity teams as AI agents become common in production environments. Those agents often need broad access to be useful, and granting it through static credentials can leave businesses with hard-to-protect secrets. The problem grows as agents interact with many APIs, applications, services and data sources, since each added system brings another authentication requirement and more operational complexity. The articles do not say how many customers use the product or what it will cost, and they do not describe any further releases.

Articles.Title: Kong launches Token Vault to secure AI agent access - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Forrester warns of shadow AI governance gap in Asia Pacific
stories.Summary:
Forrester, a research and advisory firm, published its 2027 Asia Pacific predictions report on November 9, 2026, warning that one in three large enterprises in the region will face a shadow AI agent governance problem. The firm expects large organisations to find at least 10 employee-built shadow AI agents for every officially sanctioned agent, as staff-built tools, embedded software features and locally chosen AI platforms spread faster than internal controls. Forrester says this will create a new layer of technical debt linked to unmanaged risk, weaker governance, duplicated functions and undocumented dependencies. The report argues that executives in the region should focus less on how quickly AI is deployed and more on control, governance and accountability.

The report also forecasts that one in five large regulated enterprises will approve Chinese open-weight models, reflecting a wider view of sovereignty that extends beyond data residency to control over models and inference. Greater visibility into model weights and bias could lead some firms to approve self-hosted Chinese models where they meet operational sovereignty requirements, despite lingering concerns about provenance and geopolitics. Forrester further predicts that a personal AI agent belonging to an employee will trigger an incident at a Fortune 500 company. As consumer AI use grows, more workers may bring personal agents into the office, giving them access to corporate devices, credentials and data. Existing security systems tend to verify identity and access rather than intent, so an agent performing a seemingly routine task could misuse its privileges or expose sensitive information.

Forrester also expects 10 of Asia Pacific's largest consumer-facing brands to differentiate themselves through human assurance, making human oversight standard in high-consequence interactions such as those involving financial risk, emotional vulnerability or complex decisions. Sectors like financial services and healthcare are likely to keep pairing AI-led experiences with access to human experts and licensed advisers where trust is critical. Frederic Giron, Vice President and Senior Research Director at Forrester, said the region's diversity makes governance a central issue for companies scaling AI. He said organisations that adapt governance to local sovereignty requirements while building long-term trust with customers will be better placed to capture AI's value. The report suggests governance in Asia Pacific may need to be more localised than in other regions, since companies operating across several jurisdictions must navigate different rules on data handling, model hosting and accountability.

Articles.Title: Forrester warns of shadow AI governance gap in Asia Pacific - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Australian firms not ready for AI at scale, study warns
stories.Summary:
Interactive, a technology services firm, has published research warning that few Australian organisations are ready to deploy artificial intelligence at scale. Only 8% of data and AI leaders said their data was optimised for that task, and the report was compiled by ADAPT Research & Advisory for Interactive's Unstoppable AI Blueprint. The study also found weak returns from AI agents, with just 15% of surveyed Chief Information Officers and Chief Data and AI Officers saying results met or exceeded expectations. The article was published on 10 November 2026.

The main barriers, according to the research, extend well beyond core technology systems. Among Chief Information Officers asked which areas were least mature for scaling AI, data foundations and quality ranked highest at 40%, followed by workforce capability and adoption and process design and operational readiness at 38% each. Governance and risk management scored 36% and value realisation and measurement 34%, while technology and platforms ranked last at 25%. The report also said 71% of Chief Information Officers felt their organisations were not prepared, or only slightly prepared, to manage an agentic workforce, and only 9% had enterprise-wide controls over what AI agents can access and act on.

Lizzy Jones, Head of Data and AI at Interactive, said the quality of the underlying environment determines whether AI projects produce meaningful results, because AI magnifies existing strengths and weaknesses. Chris Pallister, Head of Managed Security Services at Interactive, warned that operational risks rise quickly when autonomous systems run without clear safeguards, and he advised leaders to know what an agent can access, who owns it, and how fast it can be switched off. Interactive also described its own internal results, saying enterprise AI agents helped it onboard vendors and suppliers about 20 times faster and that AI-assisted triage cut average threat detection and response times from 40 minutes to seven. Jones credited those gains to preparing staff before rollout.

The research further found that Australian companies are reassessing where AI workloads should run amid cost pressure and infrastructure gaps. Only 9% of infrastructure leaders rated their environment as highly or fully ready for AI workloads, while 77% reported active cost pressure. Just 14% reported mature FinOps practices, and 28% planned to repatriate some public cloud workloads, up from 10% in 2020. The survey covered senior executives across data and AI, information technology, and cloud and infrastructure functions, and the article presents its findings as part of a wider pattern in which board enthusiasm for AI is outpacing the practical work on data quality, governance and cost control.

Articles.Title: Australian firms not ready for AI at scale, study warns - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Why jumping straight to an AI proof of concept is costing you
stories.Summary:
Most AI projects stall between a promising pilot and a working system, according to an article on IT Brief Australia published on 10 November 2026. The author argues that the fix is not a better model but spending the budget in the right order. The piece cites RAND Corporation's estimate that more than 80 per cent of AI projects fail, and a 2025 S&P Global Market Intelligence survey of more than 1,000 organisations in which 42 per cent had abandoned most of their AI initiatives, up from 17 per cent the year before. It also reports that the average organisation scrapped 46 per cent of its proofs of concept before they reached production.

The author says these failures usually stem from decisions made before any model is trained, not from the technology itself. RAND interviews with 65 experienced data scientists and engineers identified causes such as optimising the wrong metric, lacking enough good data, chasing new techniques over simple solutions, having no path to production, and asking AI to do things it cannot yet do. The author adds two patterns seen in Australian organisations: spending heavily before the idea is proven, and underestimating what production requires. The article proposes splitting each project into four stages, with the first three using 20 to 40 per cent of total investment to prove the idea is worth the rest.

Those stages are strategy and ideation at 5 to 10 per cent, data analysis and feasibility at 5 to 10 per cent, and a proof of concept at 10 to 20 per cent, with implementation, testing and productionising taking 60 to 80 per cent. The author recommends a readiness and feasibility assessment before any proof of concept, covering whether the data, platforms, governance and people can support the idea, along with an estimate of running costs. The article is written by the publication's contributors and presents the approach as the view of the organisation behind it. It notes that a "don't proceed" result is a valid outcome, since catching flawed assumptions early is cheaper than discovering them after months of build work.

Articles.Title: Why jumping straight to an AI proof of concept is costing you - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: C.H. Robinson expands AI into ocean, air & customs
stories.Summary:
C.H. Robinson has extended its AI systems beyond trucking into ocean shipping, air freight and customs brokerage, according to a November 9, 2026 report. The new agents now produce price quotes for ocean and air cargo, support ocean bookings and help prepare customs paperwork for shipments entering the United States. In some cases, a single shipping task requires more than a dozen AI agents working together. The company says these systems are changing how quickly and consistently it serves customers.

The clearest change is in pricing, where AI has produced more than 80,000 quotes for more than 3,600 customers. Turnaround has dropped from one day for an air shipment and two to three days for an ocean shipment to two to three minutes. Ocean booking agents now manage the thousands of booking requests the company receives each week. In customs brokerage, the systems process the many documents needed to clear US Customs, a task that has grown more labour-intensive as trade rules and tariffs have become more complex.

Mike Short, President of Global Forwarding, said the faster quoting and booking give customers information sooner and let them evaluate new routes, modes, schedules or prices more quickly when disruptions occur. Mike Neill, Chief Technology Officer, said the company still has more automation to build, noting that earlier digital booking efforts over about 10 years reached only about 5% automation for ocean and air bookings. Arun Rajan, Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer, said the company has built hundreds of proprietary AI agents since 2023 and is now using its data and in-house engineering to widen its position in global forwarding. The company reports that time spent on customs processing has so far fallen by 23%.

Freight forwarding is harder to automate than trucking because prices depend on more variables, such as origin port, terminal charges, inland transport links and destination routing, which can change often. Short gave the example of Shanghai, where an agent must first determine which of two ports a shipper means, then account for tolls and fees at 43 terminals. Separate agents check terminal websites and emails for fee changes, so staff in different time zones do not have to gather that information by phone. When a customer does not name a port, the systems can suggest options based on pickup point, sailing frequency and inland choices such as truck, rail or barge.

Articles.Title: C.H. Robinson expands AI into ocean, air & customs - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons
stories.Summary:
Microsoft Research has released threat research, reported on the Microsoft Security Blog on November 10, showing how a capable agent model could be turned into a sleeper agent. According to the research, editing fewer than 10 neurons is enough to inject a short payload into the model. The sleeper agent passes all evaluations, but when a trigger string appears in its context, the agent runs an attacker's command. Because agents now frequently run unattended with privileged system access, the article says the integrity of model weights is a security concern for both third-party and internally developed models.

The article says the attack needs only inference-only compute, since a machine with enough RAM to run a model has enough resources to weight-space backdoor it. A backdoored model runs the command with whatever access the agent has in its environment. Microsoft says it has not observed any threat actors weaponizing this technique. The article notes that the research aligns with similar recent work by Anthropic and MIT on agentic backdoors and weight-space programming, respectively. Claude Code with Opus 4.5 discovered most of this threat autonomously, according to the post.

Microsoft Research is the group behind the findings, and the post is published under Microsoft Threat Intelligence. The article states that Microsoft Research found the threat is detectable by frontier agents, which can identify anomalous weight edits. It also says Satya Nadella recently outlined an approach of independent observability and other controls for AI models and agents, in a blog post the article links. The article describes the research as demonstrating a process in which agents surface new security problems and human researchers then systematize, study, and mitigate them.

The article's mitigation guidance recommends diffing every checkpoint against its declared base model before deployment and after each update. It says implanted neurons tend to change a few weight vectors by a large amount, while legitimate fine-tunes change weights broadly and diffusely. The guidance also recommends using frontier AI agents as auditors in the model intake pipeline, and treating every third-party model as untrusted until it is audited. Microsoft further advises running agents with least privilege, executing agent-generated code only in isolated sandboxes, and requiring human approval for high-impact tool calls. The article lists Microsoft Defender tools, Azure Machine Learning registries, and Microsoft Entra Agent ID among the products it names for these controls.

Articles.Title: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons

stories.Headline: Imperial Heritage Caviar doubles time saved on administrative tasks by adding AI to its Dynamics 365 Business Central platform
stories.Summary:
Imperial Heritage Caviar, a family-owned Belgian caviar house, has added custom AI agents to its Dynamics 365 Business Central platform so that it can take and process orders more quickly. The company had already been saving an hour a day on administrative tasks with Business Central, and with the agents that time savings has more than doubled, which the company says amounts to hundreds of hours a year. The agents were built by the technical partner Deltanexx, took just a few weeks to develop, and were announced in a Microsoft customer story dated November 11, 2026. The company's owner, Elisabeth Colman, said the agents have turned data entry into a conversational process.

The agents were built because orders arrive through WhatsApp, email, SMS and phone calls, and Imperial Heritage wanted one system that could handle them all. Deltanexx built two agents, one on Microsoft Copilot Studio and one on Anthropic's Claude, so employees can use the tools they prefer. Both connect to Business Central through its MCP server and carry out three skills: creating sales orders, setting up new customer records and preparing weekly customer follow-up reports. For sales orders, the agent turns a plain-language request into customer and item records, presents them for review and asks for confirmation before creating the order. Administrators must also grant consent for the Claude connection, which is registered in the company's Microsoft Entra ID tenant, and Business Central's MCP configuration defines which operations the agent can use.

Colman estimates that manual order entry previously took one to two hours a day and now takes less than 30 minutes, with routine order preparation taking just a few seconds. She also said the agent has virtually eliminated the errors that came from entering large, complex orders quickly. Deltanexx managing partner Dhia Athmini said the agents were shaped specifically to Imperial Heritage's workflow processes. Colman said that employees can now begin preparing deliveries at the start of the day rather than first entering the orders received overnight. The company serves about 500 active customers, including three-star Michelin restaurants and a privately owned cruise ship.

Imperial Heritage is planning to extend the agents further, according to the article. Vendor and purchase order APIs are already included in the MCP configuration, which would allow Deltanexx to develop additional purchasing skills. The company wants to build on the follow-up skill to identify customers who normally order weekly or monthly but have not yet placed their next order. It is also exploring how the agent could help manage supplier price increases while limiting the effect on margins. Colman summarized the company's aim as giving staff more time to serve customers and build relationships.

Articles.Title: Imperial Heritage Caviar doubles time saved on administrative tasks by adding AI to its Dynamics 365 Business Central platform

stories.Headline: Companies must integrate AI into their customer service for real transformation - ET CIO
stories.Summary:
An EY report has concluded that adopting artificial intelligence tools alone will not be enough for companies to transform their customer service operations. Businesses instead need to redesign their operating models, technology systems and workforce capabilities to achieve meaningful results. The report urges companies to move beyond deploying individual AI applications and to integrate the technology into their existing business systems. The goal, according to the report, is better customer experience, higher productivity and greater operational efficiency.

EY describes a five-step roadmap for this transformation. The first step is assessing current operations, including business and operating models, technology infrastructure, process readiness, workforce skills and performance measurement systems. The second step is building foundations, which means strengthening customer and interaction data, improving knowledge repositories, establishing governance and risk management, and preparing employees for changes in their roles. The third step is identifying priority use cases that can improve customer experience, increase efficiency, reduce service costs and raise productivity. The fourth step is connecting AI capabilities with existing operating systems that bring together customer service, analytics, people and business platforms.

The report says the most successful organizations run customer service on integrated business systems rather than on isolated AI use cases. It also notes that the path to value from AI is not the same for every organization, which is why companies need to revisit their transformation priorities, operating models, technology choices and governance structures. The article attributes these findings to the EY report and does not name any individual author or executive. It does not say whether the report's recommendations have been adopted by any particular company.

The fifth and final step is measuring actual business outcomes rather than tracking AI adoption or the number of tasks handled by the technology. According to the report, organizations reaching the highest levels of value measure gains in cost, efficiency, customer experience, productivity and revenue. EY also stresses continuous investment in data, knowledge, governance and employee readiness so that AI-led change delivers lasting business value. The article does not say what steps, if any, are planned beyond the report's recommendations.

Articles.Title: Companies must integrate AI into their customer service for real transformation - ET CIO

stories.Headline: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
stories.Summary:
Researchers at OpenAI, working with the online freelance marketplace Upwork, published new findings on November 10, 2026, on how AI is changing freelance work. The study compared freelance job postings on Upwork with the tasks people carry out directly in ChatGPT, covering ChatGPT data from January 2025 through June 2026 and Upwork data through the first half of 2026. The authors found that demand is shifting, with some familiar services losing market share while AI-related projects bring together different capabilities. They also found that these projects tend to carry larger budgets and more hours of work. The report was released as part of OpenAI's Work at the Frontier series.

The research does not describe a new rule or requirement, but it does document several changes in the market. Writing made up a much larger share of ChatGPT use than of freelance requests, while video and animation accounted for larger shares of Upwork postings. Of 63 work categories analyzed, 43 followed the pattern in which activities common in ChatGPT use lost share on Upwork, while 20 showed the reverse. Between early 2023 and late 2025, the mix of tasks in AI-related postings became 45% more diverse, roughly the equivalent of an increase from about 15 equally common tasks to about 21. Although hourly rates were similar for AI-related and other work, AI-related projects had larger fixed-price budgets and involved more hours of work.

OpenAI's Economic Research Team and Upwork are the parties behind the findings, and the authors are careful about what their data can show. They say that ChatGPT use alone does not explain changes in freelance demand, and they point to a gap they call the capability overhang, meaning the difference between how people currently use ChatGPT and the wider range of tasks AI can support. The authors also argue that the findings do not point to a simple substitution story, since the pattern of lost share was not uniform. They suggest that AI may be shifting both what clients seek from freelancers and how they assemble projects.

They further note that freelance postings can reveal changes sooner than economy-wide employment statistics because contracts are short and clients revise requirements with each posting. The context the articles provide is that Upwork's 2026 Future Workforce Index found 38% of skilled U.S. knowledge workers freelance, and an earlier Upwork study estimated that freelance knowledge work generated $1.5 trillion in U.S. earnings in 2024. The articles do not describe any further steps, follow-up studies or policy responses that are planned. They describe the work as an early view of changes that are still developing.

Articles.Title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work

stories.Headline: EXL Acquires Aimpoint Digital, Adds 250 AI and Data Experts
stories.Summary:
EXL, the data analytics and AI services company, has acquired Aimpoint Digital, a data and AI consulting firm, to expand its forward-deployed AI engineering capabilities. The deal, reported on November 9, 2026, adds about 250 AI engineers, platform architects, analytics consultants, decision scientists and AI strategists to EXL's workforce. The companies did not disclose the financial terms of the transaction. The purpose is to help enterprises move AI projects out of pilot stages and into production.

The acquisition is meant to strengthen EXL's capabilities across the full enterprise AI lifecycle, including strategy, architecture, engineering, deployment, evaluation and managed operations. It also broadens the company's expertise across AI and data platforms such as Anthropic, Databricks and Snowflake. The combined offering is designed to give clients a single partner from initial strategy discussions through architecture, production deployment and ongoing operations. EXL said this should reduce handoffs between teams and create clearer accountability for business outcomes. Aimpoint Digital brings experience building enterprise data and AI platforms, along with engineers who work closely with client teams.

EXL's chairman and chief executive, Rohit Kapoor, said clients need a partner who can take them from AI ambition to impact at enterprise scale. He said Aimpoint Digital's strategists and engineers bring hands-on expertise to turn AI strategy into production on the platforms clients trust most. Ben Yopp, chief executive and co-founder of Aimpoint Digital, said the firm's AI strategy and engineering talent, combined with EXL's industry expertise, global reach and ability to run AI in operations, lets them take clients' most important AI initiatives into production. The acquisition comes as enterprises increase AI spending but still struggle to move projects beyond pilots.

The deal follows EXL's earlier purchase of AI model training and evaluation company iMerit, which expanded EXL's work in model training, evaluation and reinforcement learning. With Aimpoint Digital, EXL is focusing on the engineering and deployment side of its AI business, complementing the model development capabilities gained from iMerit. Together, the two acquisitions are intended to cover the AI lifecycle from model development and evaluation to enterprise deployment and managed operations. The articles do not say what further steps EXL plans beyond this integration.

Articles.Title: EXL Acquires Aimpoint Digital, Adds 250 AI and Data Experts - Analytics India Magazine

stories.Headline: India’s Office Workforce to Reach 48 Mn by 2030 as AI Reshapes Demand: Report
stories.Summary:
India's office-using workforce is projected to rise from about 38 million in 2025 to 48 million by 2030, according to a study by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield published in November 2026. Under the consultancy's baseline scenario, office employment would grow by nearly 9 million between 2025 and 2030, or about 1.8 million workers a year. The study ties this growth to the expansion of office-based services and global capability centres, which are moving toward higher-value work. The report expects those centres to drive demand for research and development, product engineering and analytics. It also says the shift toward more advanced work will raise demand for well-located, adaptable office space.

The projection comes with a warning that vacancies may rise as new commercial office supply enters the market. The study expects the national office vacancy rate to climb from 14.3 percent in 2025 to a peak of 16.2 percent in 2029, then ease to 15.5 percent in 2030 as new supply levels off. It also argues that India's lower labour costs may limit the immediate business case for AI adoption. Productivity gains from AI are expected to become more visible later in the decade, mainly in IT services and global capability centres. The report describes AI as likely to change the nature of work and the skills employers need, though not necessarily to reduce office space demand.

Anshul Jain, chief executive of Cushman & Wakefield's office and retail business for India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa, and Asia Pacific, is quoted in the study. He said AI would change the nature of work and required skills, but that this does not necessarily lower office demand. Jain also said occupiers will increasingly prioritise quality and flexibility in their office requirements. He said developers and investors will need to adapt to changing workplace needs.

The study's authorship and the consultancy's own forecasts are the source of these figures, and the article does not report any independent verification. The article does not say what happens next beyond the forecast period, nor does it describe any regulatory or policy response. It is a single consultancy study reported by one publication, so the figures reflect a baseline scenario rather than a settled outcome. The projections run through 2030, and the article gives no further timeline for how the vacancy peak or productivity gains will play out.

Articles.Title: India’s Office Workforce to Reach 48 Mn by 2030 as AI Reshapes Demand: Report - Analytics India Magazine

stories.Headline: Microsoft stock falls as Anthropic takes aim at Excel and workplace software
stories.Summary:
Microsoft shares fell about 2% on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, after Bloomberg reported that Anthropic was preparing a suite of AI-powered workplace tools aimed at Microsoft's Excel and Google's Sheets. The new products were expected to be unveiled at an Anthropic event that day. Among them is Claude Sheets, a spreadsheet service that closely resembles Excel and Google Sheets but builds Anthropic's AI capabilities directly into the application. The package also includes a video-call assistant and a data dashboard tool. The launch is seen as a possible expansion of competition for Microsoft, which has been adding AI to its Office products through its Copilot platform.

Anthropic is also widening Claude's role as a platform for third-party software, announcing a way for businesses including Adobe, Atlassian and HubSpot to embed versions of their applications within Claude. This positions Claude as an alternative interface through which customers can reach business applications, while Anthropic builds competing products of its own. The company's revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, according to its IPO filing. Anthropic is seeking a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its planned public offering. Its push into workplace software is therefore closely watched as investors judge its ability to compete beyond its established strength in AI-assisted software development.

The tension is complicated by Microsoft's own ties to Anthropic. According to the company's latest filing, Microsoft is among the companies taking part in a separate $26 billion private placement tied to Anthropic's IPO, alongside Google, Nvidia and AMD. Anthropic product leader Nicholas Lin told Bloomberg that Claude Sheets is still a relatively basic product and is not designed for sophisticated financial modeling or advanced enterprise workloads. He said the company believes its integrations with existing spreadsheet software will remain more effective for those tasks. Even so, the move signals Anthropic's ambition to capture a larger share of corporate productivity spending, an area dominated by Microsoft and Google.

Articles.Title: Microsoft stock falls as Anthropic takes aim at Excel and workplace software

stories.Headline: AI and the culture of your firm
stories.Summary:
The article reports on a conversation published by Accounting Today on November 9, 2026, in which Dan Hood, its editor-in-chief, spoke with Sandra Wiley, CEO and chief strategist of Sandra Wiley Strategies, about how artificial intelligence will change the culture of accounting firms. Hood framed the discussion as a look at an area that has received little attention, noting that both the culture firms will have and the culture they build now will shape whether they can make the most of AI. Wiley, a consultant on human capital issues such as culture, recruiting and retention, argued that the profession will need to pay closer attention to culture than it has before. Wiley said that culture is not something that simply appears but something firms can build on purpose, and that AI will shift it in several ways.

She expects trust to be extended to people earlier in their careers, because AI will take over much of the entry-level work that staff used to learn from over three to five years. She also described AI as becoming a partner to staff, so that people and technology together form one culture rather than two separate parts of the firm. Wiley added that productivity outcomes are likely to matter more than billable hours, and that firms will need different roles, profiles and hiring expectations than they have had before. Hood and Wiley agreed that the change will require a higher level of trust and knowledge at every level, including partners, many of whom may be unfamiliar with advisory work.

Wiley said that the entry point into the profession will rise, which means the ceiling of firms will rise too, and she noted that many of the young CPAs she has spoken with want challenging work from the start. Hood pointed out that training newer staff faster to earn trust sooner is a different path from what his own professors described, and that the pipeline of students and new recruits takes years to develop. Wiley said firm leaders will need to run a current firm and a future firm at the same time, and she warned that firms that do not start transforming now could face trouble within a couple of years. The conversation ended with Hood and Wiley noting that the pace of AI change is hard to match with the slower timeline of building the workforce.

Articles.Title: AI and the culture of your firm - Accounting Today

stories.Headline: QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic Use AI to Reduce Quantum Circuit Resource Requirements
stories.Summary:
Researchers from QuEra Computing, Harvard University and Anthropic reported on November 10, 2026 that AI can design quantum circuits that need fewer computational resources. The team used Claude to design circuits for eight computational building blocks, and in seven of them the AI-designed circuits reduced both gate counts and qubit requirements compared with baseline designs. The research preprint, titled "Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models" (arXiv:2610.22367), was led by Andi Gu as part of Anthropic's STEM Fellows Program. The eighth building block produced a new approach that offers additional trade-offs between qubit requirements and gate counts. The work was announced in a press release from QuEra.

The researchers paired Claude with an independent automated evaluator that checked each design for correctness and scored it on Toffoli-gate count and qubit count. The Reed-Solomon decoder, the most expensive step in decoded quantum interferometry, went from 5.1 million Toffoli gates to about 440,000, with fewer qubits used. The Coulomb potential calculation saw a 9.9-fold reduction in its combined resource metric, with Toffoli gates falling from 6,355 to 1,140 and qubits from 252 to 142. A fixed-point Gaussian function showed a 39-fold reduction in the combined metric, with Toffoli gates dropping from about 24,000 to 1,583 and qubits from 362 to 139. The combined metric multiplies Toffoli-gate count by peak logical qubits, so these figures are not speedups, and the results are resource estimates rather than hardware runs.

Beyond improving existing designs, Claude helped discover a new reversible approach to modular inversion, an arithmetic operation central to elliptic-curve calculations. In the complete point-addition benchmark, one design required about 17 times fewer gates than the prior design using the fewest qubits, while using about 12 percent more qubits. Mikhail Lukin, Co-Founder and Chief Science Officer at QuEra and a professor at Harvard, said AI guided by a rigorous evaluator found circuit structures that work more efficiently within the constraints of reversible computing. Alek Kemeny of Anthropic said the evaluator made the work possible because every design was independently checked and scored. Takuya Kitagawa, President of QuEra Computing, said AI-driven reductions in resources expand what future fault-tolerant systems can deliver.

The findings build on an earlier pilot between QuEra and Anthropic in which Claude developed and validated laser-control software. In that pilot, the software recovered the correct laser lock in 695 of 700 trials, in seconds rather than the 5 to 10 minutes a human expert needs. The article notes that successive advances reduced the estimated Toffoli-gate count for one widely studied FeMoco simulation by roughly 150,000 times over eight years. The new elliptic-curve circuit approach came from a 53-hour search guided by researcher-defined requirements and an automated evaluator. QuEra says it is building fault-tolerant quantum computers, with its Libra system targeted for availability on Amazon Braket in 2028.

Articles.Title: QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic Use AI to Reduce Quantum Circuit Resource Requirements

stories.Headline: Lens Technology to start glass substrate pilot line by year-end, eyes Korean chipmakers
stories.Summary:
China's Lens Technology plans to build and operate its first through-glass via (TGV) glass substrate pilot line by the end of 2026, according to a DIGITIMES report datelined Taipei and published on November 10, 2026. The company is seeking partnerships with South Korean semiconductor and memory companies as it moves from smartphone glass into advanced chip packaging. The article's visible text is a teaser, and the full account is behind a paid subscription. Because only the opening summary is available, the report does not give further detail on the line's capacity, investment, or partner names. The move is described as a push from Lens's existing smartphone glass business toward glass substrates used in semiconductor packaging.

The source names the pilot line as the company's first TGV glass substrate line and the target of year-end 2026 for its start. The South Korean partnership is described as the company's aim, not as a deal already signed. The article's visible text does not say what the pilot line will produce beyond that general purpose. Lens Technology is the party responsible for the plan, and the teaser attributes the plan and the search for partners to the company itself. The report credits reporters Jingyue Hsiao of DIGITIMES, with the story filed from Taipei.

Beyond that, the visible text offers no statements from company executives or from any prospective Korean partner. The surrounding DIGITIMES page lists several unrelated stories about Nvidia, memory supply, and Taiwanese chip firms, but none of them concerns Lens Technology's pilot line. The visible text does not say whether the year-end target has been met, whether any Korean company has agreed to work with Lens, or what the next steps are. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Lens Technology to start glass substrate pilot line by year-end, eyes Korean chipmakers - digitimes

stories.Headline: Nvidia scandal raises export risks for Korean chipmakers
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship with a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, whom US investigators reportedly suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. The disclosure came in an email to employees on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, in which he apologized to his family and pledged to cooperate with an internal review. The reports that prompted the scrutiny say US authorities had been looking into her former employer, Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, since 2024 over suspicions it diverted restricted Nvidia chips to China. Those intelligence suspicions have not been established as fact, and Nvidia had earlier described the contacts as routine business dealings.

The controversy could lead Washington to tighten oversight of AI chip exports through third countries, which would mean more verification of end users, intended applications and possible reexports. Such checks could raise compliance costs and delay shipments for Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, and any limits on Nvidia's sales to China could indirectly reduce demand for the high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, used in its accelerators. No new restrictions had been announced in connection with the case. Some analysts see a possible upside as Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta develop their own AI processors, which could widen the customer base for HBM. An industry official said the short-term compliance burden must be managed without losing sight of that opportunity.

Nvidia's independent directors, advised by outside counsel, will examine whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised and expressed confidence in him, and he remains CEO. Three US House committee chairs have asked for a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 about his contacts with Alice Huang and the company's safeguards against espionage. South Korea's government said Monday it expects Nvidia GPU deliveries under existing contracts to proceed as scheduled, while Vice Science Minister Ryu Je-myung said the investigation's impact remains uncertain.

The episode also drew attention to the leadership question at Nvidia, which commands 80% to 90% of the GPU market. One report noted that a possible divorce could affect Huang's stake of about 3.58 percent, and that the company lacks a formal CEO succession plan. Separately, Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter and a senior Nvidia executive, canceled a planned visit to Seoul that included meetings with officials and the Korean AI chipmaker Rebellions. Nvidia's AI Day in Seoul went ahead on Monday and Tuesday with Vice President Deepu Talla taking her place at a startup partnership forum. Korean markets were also under pressure, with the KOSPI closing at 5,018.85 after a third straight decline.

Articles.Title: Spy Scandal and Stake Risk Hit Nvidia, Rattling Korean HBM Chain - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute Wins International AI Standard
stories.Summary:
The Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute announced on November 10, 2026 that it has obtained ISO/IEC 42001 certification, the international standard for artificial intelligence management systems. The institute says it is the first public institution under the Korea Forest Service to receive the certification. The standard was set in December 2023 by the International Organization for Standardization and the International Electrotechnical Commission as the world's first such standard for AI management. It assesses whether an organization manages risk, transparency and accountability when it adopts and runs AI. The institute says the certification recognizes its framework and capacity for using AI safely and responsibly.

To meet the standard, the institute has widened its use of AI in public services and internal work tied to arboreta and gardens. It set up AI operating policies and internal management rules, and it added a risk assessment procedure for each AI system. It also raised the quality controls on data used to train and run AI, strengthened protection of personal data, and spelled out which units and roles handle this work. The institute plans to review and improve its AI management framework on a regular basis. Its stated aims are to prevent risks that may arise from AI use and to offer AI services that the public can trust.

The institute's chairman, Sim Sang-taek, is the official who framed the announcement. According to the report, he said the institute will keep providing better arboreta and garden services through transparent and trustworthy AI operations. The article was written by Park Hee-yoon for Seoul Economic Daily and was translated from Korean with AI, so the quotations may not match the original wording exactly. The report does not describe any reaction from outside observers or any penalties or deadlines tied to the certification.

Articles.Title: Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute Wins International AI Standard - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: NH-Amundi Lists ETF Tracking AI Chip Substrate Suppliers
stories.Summary:
NH-Amundi Asset Management said on November 10, 2026, that it had listed the HANARO Samsung Electro-Mechanics Fixed AI Core Substrate ETF on the main board of the Korea Exchange. The fund targets makers of multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) and high-value package substrates, such as flip-chip ball grid arrays (FC-BGA), which are needed in growing volumes as AI systems advance. Samsung Electro-Mechanics, which mass-produces both MLCCs and FC-BGAs, is the anchor holding at a fixed 25% weighting. The remaining 75% is spread across nine Korean companies in the substrate, materials and equipment chain.

Individual holdings are capped at 20%. The fund rebalances back to the 25% target at quarterly scheduled reviews if the anchor's weight drifts with share prices. The nine other stocks are chosen by an AI system built on a large language model, which analyzes corporate filings, news reports and analyst research to score how closely each company ties to the MLCC and substrate industries. Selection combines that thematic score with market capitalization.

As of the end of October, the largest holdings after Samsung Electro-Mechanics were LG Innotek, Doosan, Isu Petasys and Daeduck Electronics, followed by Simmtech, Korea Circuit, Taesung, TLB and Haesung DS. The eligible universe includes makers of package substrates and multilayer boards, plus suppliers of materials and equipment used in substrate production. NH-Amundi Asset Management, led by Chief Executive Kil Jung-sup, launched the product, and Kim Seung-chul, head of its ETF investment division, explained the rationale. Kim said that as AI accelerators and high-performance servers gain computing power, high-capacity MLCCs and ultra-fine substrates that keep power efficiency stable grow more important.

He described the fund as a one-stop vehicle for the whole domestic AI substrate value chain, anchored by Samsung Electro-Mechanics, which he called globally competitive. The articles do not report investor demand, fees or first-day trading results. The launch is framed as a response to surging demand for these components as AI servers become more powerful. The articles do not describe any regulatory action or further steps beyond the listing and the scheduled quarterly reviews.

Articles.Title: NH-Amundi Lists ETF Tracking AI Chip Substrate Suppliers - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Nvidia scandal adding to investor caution over AI
stories.Summary:
Fox Business senior correspondent Charlie Gasparino and New York Post columnist Miranda Devine discussed a scandal involving Nvidia on the program Kudlow, broadcast on November 10, 2026. The discussion centered on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. The segment was framed as a factor adding to investor caution over artificial intelligence. The articles provide no details of any new rule, requirement, or change arising from the matter.

They do not name any regulator, filing, legal action, or policy response. The only specifics available are the date of the broadcast, the names of the two commentators, and the nature of the allegation as described by them. The allegation concerns Jensen Huang, whom the segment identifies as Nvidia's chief executive. The articles describe the relationship as alleged and the individual as suspected, and they do not report any finding, charge, or statement from Nvidia or Huang in response.

The account comes solely from the broadcast summary and does not attribute any further claims to specific sources. The articles offer no further context about the wider investor reaction or the company's share price. They also do not say what, if anything, will happen next. More to follow.

stories.Headline: iH to Install AI Safety System at New Incheon Housing Complex
stories.Summary:
Incheon Metropolitan City Development Corporation, known as iH, announced on November 10, 2026, that it will install an artificial intelligence-based safety system in its public housing to protect residents from accidents. The move follows recent fires in apartment underground parking garages that heightened residents' anxieties. The agency said the system will be adopted from the design stage of its apartment project at the S2 block in Geomam, Seo District, Incheon. The measure targets everyday spaces such as electric-vehicle charging stations, children's playgrounds, and walkways within the complex.

The system will sound an alarm at an integrated control center, display live footage, and send an immediate text message to managers when an accident occurs or warning signs appear. Electric-vehicle charging stations will get three-stage temperature detection and cutoff technology, which automatically cuts power if the temperature rises above 25 degrees Celsius during charging. Flame and smoke detectors will also be installed in the parking garage. AI-enabled cameras at playgrounds and walkways will detect abnormal behavior such as falls, fainting, or assaults and alert the control room in real time. The system is scheduled to begin full operation when the complex is completed in December 2030.

iH is holding working-level meetings with the Keryong Construction consortium, the builder, to coordinate detailed safety standards. Kim Hak-jong, head of iH's housing welfare division, said that creating a living environment where residents can live with peace of mind is the basic duty of public housing. He said the agency will expand the AI smart safety system to all apartment development projects it pursues going forward, starting with the Geomam complex. The article does not say what the system will cost or how many cameras and sensors will be installed. It also gives no further details on how the expansion will be carried out across other projects.

Articles.Title: iH to Install AI Safety System at New Incheon Housing Complex - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Nvidia Supplies 90% of AI Servers. Spy Scandal Tests Its Governance
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has acknowledged an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy, a disclosure made on the 8th, local time. The allegations concern whether national secrets were leaked, and the matter has rattled the global chip industry. Huang has said he intends to stay on as chief executive, though lawmakers are pressing for an inquiry. Nvidia's graphics processing units power an estimated 80 to 90 percent of the world's data center servers, which is why the episode has drawn wide attention.

Congressional committees have asked Huang to appear in a closed session on the 18th, the day after Nvidia's scheduled earnings release on the 17th. Sen. Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, said he would pursue an investigation. Nvidia has denied any leak of secrets, and its spokesman said the matter will not slow the company's progress. The company's board plans its own probe through an independent body to examine whether trade secrets reached China and whether any transfer was careless or deliberate.

The company itself is a point of concern because it depends so heavily on one person. About 60 executives report directly to Huang, who monopolizes decision-making, and Nvidia has no formal succession plan. Huang's daughter and son both hold senior roles, and The Information reported that the company was moving toward family management, though the line of succession remains unclear. Analysts such as Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein have described Huang as the company itself. Huang has admitted fault in a letter to employees while saying he would work to win back trust.

Possible outcomes include a board request for Huang to resign or a voluntary departure, along with a criminal inquiry the articles say is a real possibility. A divorce filing could also force a property split, since Forbes estimates his net worth at $154 billion. South Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have voiced concern that the affair could prompt tighter U.S. export controls on AI chips to China. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun on the 9th called reports that Huang's partner was a Chinese spy baseless and a smear.

Articles.Title: Nvidia Supplies 90% of AI Servers. Spy Scandal Tests Its Governance - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Google Taps AMD Chips for New AI Processors Built for Agents
stories.Summary:
Google on the 9th unveiled two new artificial intelligence chips, the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i MAX, aligning its hardware with the shift toward AI agents, which are assistants that carry out tasks automatically. The company said its 8th-generation TPU lineup had grown from two chips to four, with the TPU 8t and TPU 8i unveiled in April this year joined by the two new models. It was the first time Google released four TPUs in a single year. Starting with the 8th generation, Google has split its chips by purpose, into training and inference versions. Google Cloud, a unit of Alphabet, announced the chips on the same day.

The TPU 8tx is designed for agent security and small-scale training and inference while protecting personal data, with built-in security functions that protect sensitive data in real time on the chip itself. The TPU 8i MAX links two TPU 8i chips, which are optimized for low-latency inference, and delivers twice the computing performance and memory bandwidth of the TPU 8i. The most notable element is Google's use of AMD's 5th-generation EPYC central processing unit, code-named Turin, in the TPU 8tx host infrastructure. AMD said this makes the TPU 8tx the first TPU system to offer hardware-based confidential computing. Google's Arm-based Axion CPU, unveiled in April 2024, had previously been its main choice for CPUs.

Google Cloud vice president of AI and computing infrastructure Mark Lohmeyer said customers need confidence that their data is securely protected when they deploy AI agents. He said that pairing 5th-generation EPYC processors with the 8th-generation TPU architecture has, for the first time, brought hardware-based confidential computing to Cloud TPUs. AMD has been strengthening the security features of its EPYC chips through its AMD Infinity Guard software, and said the collaboration combines EPYC performance, that security and x86 software compatibility with TPUs. The article reads the choice as a sign that EPYC is seen as ahead on security.

The move comes as AMD's standing in the server CPU market grows at Intel's expense. According to Mercury Research, Intel's share of x86 server CPU revenue was 53.8% in the first quarter of this year, while AMD reached an all-time high of 46.2%. Some observers say AMD could expand its influence further if it moves aggressively into custom chips through partnerships such as the one with Google. The article does not say what further steps Google or AMD plan beyond these announcements.

Articles.Title: Google Taps AMD Chips for New AI Processors Built for Agents - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Commvault CEO on AI security, Nvidia, data recovery
stories.Summary:
Commvault CEO Sanjay Mirchandani appeared on CNBC's "Power Lunch" on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in an interview that ran from 2:42 p.m. Eastern time. The segment covered AI agents that have gone rogue, the company's partnerships with Nvidia, and data recovery. The video listing identifies the interview only by these topics and does not describe any specific incident or event involving the company.

The article gives no further detail on what the rogue AI agents did or how Commvault's Nvidia partnership works, so those points cannot be filled in from the material provided. The listing also includes a list of other videos from the same program, mostly featuring executives from utility and energy companies discussing electricity demand and data center growth. Those related segments are not about Commvault and do not add facts about its products or customers. No new requirements, dates for changes, or regulatory actions are stated in the article.

Mirchandani is responsible for the remarks in the interview, and the article presents him as speaking for Commvault. The listing does not include any paraphrased or quoted statements from him, so his specific views on AI security or recovery are unavailable here. The CNBC description frames the discussion as a conversation about AI agents and data protection, rather than reporting a confirmed breach or outage. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Commvault CEO on AI security, Nvidia, data recovery

stories.Headline: Microsoft Warns a New Trade Crackdown Could Derail America's AI Boom
stories.Summary:
Microsoft has urged the Trump administration to drop a planned restriction on Chinese-made optical transceivers, according to a November 10 Reuters report cited by GuruFocus and Yahoo Finance. The company has lobbied administration officials against an import ban being developed by the Federal Communications Commission. The move was reported on November 10, 2026. The dispute centers on components that connect servers, networking switches and other equipment through high-speed fiber-optic cables.

The proposed ban would restrict these devices because the administration worries that Chinese-made components could enable espionage, malware installation or disruptions to critical American infrastructure. The article notes that China accounts for roughly two-thirds of the global optical transceiver market, according to Counterpoint Research. American manufacturers Coherent and Lumentum offer competing products but currently lack sufficient production capacity to replace Chinese suppliers. One possible compromise would restrict only advanced transceivers capable of transmitting 3.2 terabits per second, which are not expected to enter large-scale production until 2028. The article identifies the FCC's final decision as the most important near-term catalyst.

Microsoft is the company pressing the issue, and the article says it raised supply-chain concerns during September meetings with White House and National Security Council officials. The company has 35 data centers under construction across the United States and another 134 planned, according to market intelligence firm Cleanview. Microsoft's position is that a broad ban could increase construction costs and delay AI deployments. The administration's stated concern, as described in the article, is national security.

The article places the dispute within a broader vulnerability, since large technology companies' AI investments still depend on Chinese components that domestic manufacturers cannot quickly replace. Investors are told to watch whether restrictions target existing products or future generations, and how Azure revenue growth and data center utilization respond. The article suggests a narrowly targeted restriction could preserve Microsoft's expansion plans while broader restrictions could leave expensive AI processors underutilized. The FCC's final decision on the matter is still pending, and the article does not say when it will be issued.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Warns a New Trade Crackdown Could Derail America's AI Boom

stories.Headline: Google Taps AMD CPUs for New AI Chips Despite In-House Push
stories.Summary:
Google introduced two new artificial intelligence chips on November 9, 2026, as part of an effort to align its hardware with the growing use of AI agents, which are assistants that carry out tasks on their own. The chips are the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i MAX, and they bring the company's 8th-generation TPU family to four products, up from two announced in April. The TPU 8tx is built for small-scale training and inference while protecting personal data, with security functions on the chip itself that guard sensitive information in real time. The TPU 8i MAX links two TPU 8i chips, which are optimized for low-latency inference, to double computing performance and memory bandwidth compared with a single TPU 8i.

The most notable element is that the TPU 8tx uses AMD's 5th-generation EPYC central processing unit, code-named Turin, as its host CPU, which coordinates data movement for the GPU-style processors. AMD said these processors power the host infrastructure of the TPU 8tx, which is the first TPU system to offer hardware-based confidential computing. The move is a departure for Google, which in April 2024 had unveiled its own Arm-based CPU, Axion, and had been installing it alongside its TPUs across its data centers to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs and Intel CPUs. Google Cloud, the unit of Alphabet that leads chip development and data center construction, announced the new products.

Mark Lohmeyer, vice president of AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud, said customers need confidence that their data is securely protected when they deploy AI agents. He said that pairing the 5th-generation EPYC processors with Google's 8th-generation TPU architecture has brought hardware-based confidential computing to Cloud TPUs for the first time. AMD, for its part, said the collaboration combines EPYC performance, its AMD Infinity Guard security software and x86 software compatibility with TPUs. The articles present the choice as reflecting a judgment that EPYC is ahead on security, though that interpretation comes from the reporting rather than from either company.

The shift comes as AMD's position in server CPUs strengthens at Intel's expense. According to Mercury Research, Intel's share of x86 server CPU revenue was 53.8% in the first quarter of this year, while AMD reached an all-time high of 46.2%. Some observers quoted in the reporting suggested AMD could expand its influence further by supplying custom chips through partnerships like the one with Google, in addition to general-purpose CPUs. The articles do not say whether Google will continue to rely on its own Axion chips in other parts of its infrastructure.

Articles.Title: Google Taps AMD CPUs for New AI Chips Despite In-House Push - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Chinese AI Matchmaker Refunds Fees If You Don't Marry in 3 Years
stories.Summary:
A Chinese artificial intelligence matchmaking service is attracting attention for offering a full refund of membership fees to users who do not marry within three years. Liangpei AI launched the service in July, and Hong Kong's South China Morning Post and other foreign media reported on it on the 9th. Members pay 2,000 yuan, roughly 400,000 to 410,000 won, and can recover the full amount if they have not married after three years. The company holds the fees in a separate bank account and says it will not record them as revenue until the refund window closes.

The service differs from typical dating apps in both its goal and its structure. Instead of keeping users logged in and chatting, it aims to help them find a spouse quickly and leave the platform. New members spend about 20 minutes in a voice conversation with an AI that covers family, upbringing, education, work, interests, personality and views on marriage. The system then scores compatibility and offers one candidate at a time, and a member must end the current connection before seeing the next match. Applicants must give their real names and photographs and pass a check that they are single, and the company says that in the first month its verification screened out more than 150 married people trying to join.

Founder Zeng Xinxun created the service because, in his view, existing apps show only limited details such as age and occupation, which makes it hard to judge a person's real character. He argued that a longer conversation with an AI can capture personality, daily habits, family background and marriage expectations. He also said that having too many options may mean the algorithm has failed to identify a suitable match. The company's refund window reflects its own research, since its team surveyed 150 couples at a Shenzhen marriage registration office and found that more than 70% had married within three years of first meeting.

The service comes amid a slump in China's marriage market, which the articles tie to a tough job market and high housing and child-rearing costs. China registered 6.76 million marriages last year, up 10.8% from a year earlier but about half the 12.25 million recorded in 2015, according to Ministry of Civil Affairs data. Registrations in the first half of this year fell 7.5% from a year earlier to 3.28 million. The company said it had more than 9,300 active users as of September, 57% men and 43% women, while SCMP later reported that sign-ups had topped 35,000 with about 9% becoming paying members. The company has also raised 15 million yuan, roughly 3 billion won, in angel funding.

Articles.Title: Chinese AI Matchmaker Refunds Fees If You Don't Marry in 3 Years - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Security AI Agent Outperforms GPT and Claude
stories.Summary:
Cogent Security, a California-based AI security startup, drew attention this month after its model VR-1.1 outperformed models from Anthropic and OpenAI on a public benchmark. The article, published by The Elec on November 9, 2026, reports that VR-1.1 scored 57.9 percent accuracy across 190 CVEs on LiveCVEBench. Claude Code, powered by Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, and Codex, based on OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Cyber, each reached 45.3 percent. A CVE is a system of unique identifiers assigned to publicly disclosed software and hardware security vulnerabilities.

The benchmark measures how well AI coding agents can independently analyze and fix CVEs. VR-1.1 begins by reading vulnerability reports and source code, then generates test code to reproduce the flaw. Once the flaw is reproduced, it traces the affected code paths and applies a targeted patch. It then runs a separate review to check for new weaknesses and generates regression tests to prevent the bug from returning.

The company's cofounders include two former employees of Abnormal Security, an AI-based email security firm, and a third founder with experience at Coinbase and Blackstone. Cogent says every patch includes diagnostic results, proof-of-concept code and records of executed tests so security teams can review fixes quickly. The article notes, however, that VR-1.1 was less efficient on cost, using about 2.23 million tokens and 31 turns per successful task. Claude Code used about 380,000 tokens and 8.4 turns, and Codex used about 684,000 tokens and 15.3 turns.

The article cautions that these results come from a single benchmark and do not establish overall superiority. LiveCVEBench is designed to stop models from memorizing published answers, so it compares against baseline model versions trained before the relevant CVEs were disclosed. Newer models may have absorbed recent patch records and open-source commits into their training data, so results could differ on newly disclosed CVEs. The article also notes that when accuracy is tied, the agent using fewer tokens ranks higher.

Articles.Title: Security AI Agent Outperforms GPT and Claude - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Sakana AI Targets Record Japanese IPO, Seeking to Top Mercari's 2018 Benchmark
stories.Summary:
Sakana AI, a Japanese generative AI startup, is preparing for a possible initial public offering as early as fall 2027, according to a November 10, 2026 report from BusinessKorea. The listing could become one of the largest IPOs in Japan's startup history and would be the first by a Japanese company specializing in generative AI. Market expectations cited in the report suggest its market capitalization on the first day of trading could exceed 680 billion yen, about $4.3 billion, the benchmark set by Mercari in 2018. The venue, timing, offering size and valuation have not been finalized.

The company has selected Goldman Sachs as an IPO adviser and is in discussions with Daiwa Securities and SMBC Nikko Securities. It is considering a listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange or Nasdaq. Sakana AI says it will use the proceeds to develop its own Japanese AI models, recruit talent and expand sales. Its model, tentatively named Sakana Sawara, is slated for a smaller release in spring 2027 before a larger version follows, and the company aims to lift annualized revenue above 30 billion yen in 2027, roughly ten times its projected 2026 figure. The report notes that annualized revenue is an extrapolation of a period's revenue over a full year rather than actual revenue earned.

The article identifies Sakana AI's leadership as the company's founders, David Ha and Llion Jones, former Google AI researchers, and Ren Ito, a former Mercari executive. Their stated strategy centers on "AI sovereignty," keeping technology and operations within Japan, and on combining existing open-source models with evolutionary techniques to reach high performance with fewer computing resources. The report says the company's current product, Sakana Fugu, depends on overseas foundation models, which is why it is building Sawara to conduct its own pre-training. Clients named include MUFG Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. and Sumitomo Corp., and in July 2026 the company signed a proof-of-concept contract with Japan's Ministry of Defense.

The company was founded in 2023 and became a unicorn about a year later. In November 2025 it was valued at about 400 billion yen in a funding round involving Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and other investors, and it has drawn investment from Nvidia and Google. The article warns that global investor sentiment is a risk to the IPO, pointing to uncertainty over AI regulation and data center investment following the U.S. midterm elections, along with possible shifts in funding and listing plans at companies such as Anthropic. It adds that the company's ability to show its own model performs well and is commercially viable is likely to be a key factor in its prospects.

Articles.Title: Sakana AI Targets Record Japanese IPO, Seeking to Top Mercari's 2018 Benchmark - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: Micron Halts Taiwan Fab Construction, Facing Union Demand for 15% Profit Share
stories.Summary:
Micron Technology has effectively halted construction of Fab 11E, a new memory chip plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan, amid a wage dispute with local unions. According to Bloomberg and other foreign media reports from November 6, the company's executives suspended the project and notified Taiwanese officials and suppliers. The facility, which broke ground in July, was meant to produce high-bandwidth memory and advanced DRAM, with an investment of $3 billion to $4.5 billion, roughly 4 trillion to 6 trillion won, and operations scheduled for 2028. Only limited site-safety work continues for now.

The dispute centers on how to share profits from the AI-driven boom. Last month Micron reached a deal with the larger Taichung-based union that raised engineers' pay substantially. The Taoyuan union, which represents about 3,000 workers, rejected those terms and wants full renegotiation. Citing practices at Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, it is demanding a permanent system that distributes 15% of operating profit in cash to employees worldwide, starting in fiscal 2027, along with a special bonus that the union estimates at about 83 months of salary per employee. The union has also secured the legal right to strike, with 99.1% of voting participants backing strike authorization.

Micron's shares fell nearly 17% in the previous Nasdaq session, though the drop was not caused by the Taiwan news alone. Concerns about AI data center construction, power supply and regulation after the U.S. midterm elections also weighed on semiconductor stocks such as Nvidia and AMD. Taiwan produces about 60% of Micron's DRAM and employs around 15,000 people there, and the company has invested close to $50 billion on the island over several decades. Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs has offered to mediate with the Ministry of Labor, while Micron says its existing Taiwan lines continue to operate normally.

The two sides were scheduled to hold their fifth round of talks on November 6, but the timeline for resuming construction remains uncertain. Analysts quoted in the coverage say a prolonged delay could complicate efforts to expand next-generation memory supply for customers such as Nvidia. Micron has separately committed to investing $250 billion in U.S. manufacturing and is expanding in Japan and Singapore. Whether the talks produce an agreement will determine when work on the Taiwan plant can restart.

Articles.Title: Micron Halts Taiwan Fab Construction, Facing Union Demand for 15% Profit Share - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: Elvis Presley rights holders sue AI music generator over licensing, copyright violations
stories.Summary:
Elvis Presley Enterprises leads a group of plaintiffs who have sued Suno, an artificial intelligence music generator, claiming the company used The King's name, image and likeness along with copyrighted works without permission. The complaint was filed on a Friday in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, and the article, published November 9, 2026, reports it. The plaintiffs say Suno trained its models on protected materials and let users generate songs that imitate Presley's distinctive voice. A second group, known as the Raleigh plaintiffs, who control hundreds of other songs including Chubby Checker's 1955 hit "Let's Twist Again," joined the suit. Together the two groups say Suno infringed on 859 combined works.

The plaintiffs rely on Tennessee's Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security Act, commonly called the ELVIS Act, which extends state protection against unauthorized use of a person's likeness to include their voice. They also allege direct copyright infringement, violations of Tennessee's common law right of publicity, circumvention of copyright protection measures, and removal or alteration of copyright management information. They ask the court for an injunction barring further infringement, an order requiring Suno to destroy unauthorized copies, including those in data sets, and a complete record of its training data, plus damages for both groups. The complaint includes nearly 50 recorded examples that the plaintiffs say show Suno's outputs directly infringing on Presley's likeness and their copyrights.

The plaintiffs argue that Suno made false public statements, saying the platform does not reproduce specific melodies from others' songs and has never allowed prompts for specific artists or copyrighted songs. Their complaint contends the recorded examples contradict those assertions, and it accuses Suno of acting intentionally, maliciously and fraudulently for financial gain. Suno did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A representative for the plaintiffs, Lark-Marie Antón, said the complaint and its exhibits speak for themselves and that the rights to Presley's name, image, likeness and music are protected vigorously. Attorneys from Adams & Reese and Skaggs Faucette represent both groups.
